_meta.v2Note: Adds movement.dowseBudgetMilli (world-stage W30). A dowser sees four lanes out (Prospecting.DowserSightLanes) against a scout's two, so it costs more of the march than Scout's own 500 (half a turn) -- 250 (a quarter) is a starting value, not a measured one: it is the number a balance pass moves first.
_meta.v3Note: Adds growth and seasons (world-map W42, spec-sector-development.md). Schema-only: every growth pulse/multiplier ships at its identity value (seatPulsePerWeek 0, both multipliers 1000-per-mille) and every season multiplier ships at 1000-per-mille, so nothing downstream moves a hash -- W43-W49 wire the mechanism against these identity numbers, and W58 is the single later publish that turns them on (TurnEngine.RulesetVersion 5 -> 6, ask-first per the spec's own boundaries). growth.legionTarget is the one exception: it is the real, already-decided calibration target (world-stage-ideal.md SS8e.3), read only by the acceptance harness (W59), never by the engine -- a legion count the engine enforced would be a hard progression ceiling (AGENTS.md). raiseCostPoints and seasons.count/monthsPerSeason are provisional placeholders in the LoamPolicy sense (LoamPolicy.cs:5-9): they give the harness something to run against; picking them well is the harness's job, not this task's.
_meta.v4Note: Adds growth.raiseMemberHp (world-map W51, spec-sector-development.md SS1). A raised legion is one Fighter member at level 1; its species comes from the sector's climate (CreatureSpeciesCatalog.ElementPrimary, filtered zombie-side, picked deterministically by SpeciesId), never a new selection mechanism. 110 matches the shipped templates' own per-member Hp (WorldTemplateCatalog.cs) -- a provisional placeholder in the same LoamPolicy sense as raiseCostPoints, not a harness-tuned number. This is a schema-only addition: RecruitStock stays 0 in every shipped scenario until W58 turns growth on, so no `raise` order can ever afford to resolve today and this value moves no golden.
